title: The MAGA Internet Meltdown Down Over Epstein w/ Brace Belden
content:
Jeffrey Epstein is back in the news after a massive new cache of emails and text messages was released last week. Now, Congress has passed legislation to compel the Justice Department to release even more records. The whole saga has become a messy political fight that’s causing chaos in the MAGA movement and warping the right wing internet.

No one knows the Epstein saga better than my friend Brace Belden, co-host of the Trueanon podcast and one of the internet’s foremost experts on Epstein and MAGA influencers.

He joined my podcast this week to break down what this latest Epstein cache reveals, the real tea on Donald Trump and Bill Clinton’s relationship, and how off this Epstein stuff might impact Trump and the influencers in his movement going forward. WATCH NOW!

User Mag news rundown

  • Investors can now make bets on the price of Labubus as StockX partners with Kalshi.

  • This incredible AI generated Charlie Kirk tribute song has nearly 100k monthly listeners on Spotify.

  • ChatGPT is rolling out a new group chat feature.

  • 90% of the powdered matcha on store shelves isn’t technically matcha at all.

  • Erewhon’s Hailey Bieber smoothie is no longer named after Hailey Bieber. It’s now called the “Strawberry Glaze Skin Smoothie.”

  • OnlyFans mega star model Ari Kytsya was invited to the University of Washington to speak to a Psych 201 class of 1,200 students.

  • 97% of people detained by ICE in Chicago had no criminal record.

  • MrBeast’s new theme park in Saudi Arabia doesn’t look very impressive:

  • Nicki Minaj spoke at the United Nations about the alleged persecution of Christians in Nigeria.

  • Google’s pivot to AI cut music website Stereogum’s ad revenue by 70% overnight.

  • Fox News has hired Palantir to build a suite of AI newsroom tools.

  • TikTok will let you choose how much AI-generated content you want to see.

  • Jeff Bezos is becoming co-CEO of an AI startup that just raised $6.2 billion.

  • TurboTax is about to be integrated into ChatGPT, where customers will be guided through tasks tied to their tax filings and financial profile by the AI chatbot.

  • Quarter zips are going viral across the country after young Black men on TikTok began ditching their Nike tech tracksuits for quarter zips, embracing the high brow lifestyle that comes with the QZ like sipping matcha and LinkedIn networking.

  • Elon Musk renamed his anti-woke Wikipedia clone Grokipedia, Encyclopedia Galactica.

  • Nathan Fielder is on Raya.

  • More and more Americans can’t afford McDonald’s.

  • Scientists in Switzerland are trying to build robots in your bloodstream the size of a grain of sand that could deliver drugs with greater precision.

  • There’s been a 22-point drop in teen girls’ desire to get married over the past three decades.

  • The Charlie Kirk purge: How 600 Americans were fired, suspended, or disciplined by employers in a pro-Trump crackdown on online speech.

  • Meta is not an illegal monopoly in social networking, a judge ruled, because it competes with TikTok and YouTube. The judge also basically said it doesn’t even matter if Meta monopolized social networking, because social networking is dead.

  • Cashmere bandanas are the new hot winter neckwear.

  • A flood of conservative young men are converting to Orthodox Christianity.

  • The DoorDash delivery girl who filmed a man passed out with his pants down in his home and posted it on TikTok during a food delivery has been arrested on 2 felony charges. She is being charged with unlawful surveillance and dissemination of surveillance images.

  • Elon Musk says that after the launch of his Optimus humanoid robots jobs will no longer exist, as shareholders approved his $1 trillion pay package.

  • More pedestrians are being hit by cars and fewer are surviving.

  • Nine crew members from India and Sri Lanka who sailed aboard the container shipped that crashed into Francis Scott Key Bridge in March 2024 are *still* in Baltimore and they aren’t allowed to leave. “They’re struggling emotionally”

  • No one knows how many people die in Mississippi’s jails, because local law enforcement agencies find reporting requirements burdensome, state officials say.

  • Tesla got the green light to launch robotaxis in Arizona. (You could not pay me to ride in one!)

  • If you saw Tate McCrae’s show last week, you were exposed to measles.

  • The Financial Times is on Substack now.

  • For $8,000, you can send your teenager to live in a college dorm for a month with zero technology access to help them break their screen time habit.
